purpose: One or more fill-in-the-blank code exercises on a single slide. Learner types answers into inline <input> fields embedded in a code block. Check/hint/wrong-answer UI is fully automatic — never build any of it by hand.

first_arg.accepts: a single item object, OR an array of item objects (stacked on one slide, each with its own Check/hint/score, sharing the slide's single Reset button)

item_object_shape.code: REQUIRED string. The code template. Mark each blank with __id__ (double underscore, an alphanumeric id, double underscore — e.g. "ch __send__ 42"). The surrounding static text is plain code text (NOT HTML — no need to escape < > & here even though the underlying code sits inside a <pre><code>, escaping is handled internally); write real Go/JS/etc syntax as-is, including bare < and > and &.
item_object_shape.blanks: REQUIRED array of { id, answer }. Every __id__ used in `code` needs a matching entry here with the same id (string) and the expected `answer` (string). Answer comparison is case-insensitive and trims surrounding whitespace, but is otherwise exact-match (no partial credit, no regex).
item_object_shape.explain:
REQUIRED string. Shown after Check is pressed. Rendered as INNERHTML (real HTML, unconditionally) —
, , 
, etc. all work here directly, no opt-in flag needed. Escape < > & yourself for anything not meant to be a tag.
item_object_shape.lang: OPTIONAL string. One of: go | js | html | css | bash | docker | yml | json | generic. When set, the STATIC (non-blank) parts of `code` are auto-colored with the same tokenizer/colors as a manual class="lang-go" block. The <input> elements for the blanks themselves are never colored/affected — they stay plain form inputs regardless of `lang`. Omitting `lang` renders the whole code block in plain, uncolored monospace (the original/default look).

first_arg.array_form_example: addFillBlank([item1, item2], opts?) — both items appear stacked on one slide.

opts_object.label: string. Overrides the default slide header text (default is "Fill in the Blank").
opts_object.note: string, Greek. Short instructional line under the header.
opts_object.bg: string, image path — same shared #slide-bg-layer background mechanism as every other add* function.

no_allowHTML_here: addFillBlank has no opts.allowHTML — it doesn't need one. `code` is plain text by nature (it's code, not prose), and `explain` is already unconditionally HTML. The only opt-in toggle for this function is the per-item `lang` field described above.

automatic_ui_behavior.input_sizing: Each blank <input> auto-grows/shrinks its width to fit typed content (minimum ~4 characters wide).
automatic_ui_behavior.hint_button: Labeled 'Reveal hint (N/total)'. Each click reveals ONE random still-empty blank's correct answer as plain text below the code (never says which specific blank it belongs to — the learner has to match it themselves). Once every blank is revealed, the button becomes disabled and reads 'Everything Shown'. If the item has only 1 blank total, the button is replaced by a disabled '[Time to Guess]' label instead (revealing the only blank would just be handing over the answer).
automatic_ui_behavior.check_button: Grades every blank at once (case-insensitive, trimmed exact match). Correct blanks get a green outline; wrong ones get a red diagonal strike through the input plus the correct answer floating above it in green. After Check, all inputs and the hint button become disabled — one attempt per item (Reset clears it for a retry).
automatic_ui_behavior.hint_button_position: Always rendered ABOVE the growing list of revealed hints, so its position never shifts as you click it repeatedly.

scoring: Automatic. 100 if fully correct with zero hints used. 50 if fully correct but at least one hint was revealed (regardless of how many). 0 if any blank is wrong. A 'Score: N%' badge appears next to the slide's Reset button.
